question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to $\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{x}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$ for $0\le x<4\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{5\pi }{6}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our two equations for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6}+2\cdot 2n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =2\cdot \frac{5\pi }{6}+2\cdot 2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+4n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{5\pi }{3}+4n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{12n\pi }{3} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{5\pi }{3}+\frac{12n\pi }{3} \\ x & =\frac{(12n+1)\pi }{3} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(12n+5)\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<4\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ and $x=\frac{5\pi }{3}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<4\pi .$ So, the solutions are $x=\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{5\pi }{3}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot \frac{5\pi }{3}=\frac{5{\pi }^{2}}{9}.
$$
